patterns.summary: Turn invisible until you attack or are detected
Take over an enemy vehicle by throwing out or killing its crew
patterns.hint: Jarmen Kell's fit_note asks for a crew-kill variant: kill a vehicle's crew from range and leave the empty hull neutral for anyone to claim; the Sentry Drone and the Battle Bus are immune to it. Decide whether this is a variant of hijack-vehicle or needs its own id.

patterns.summary: Your attacks or an aura tag enemy soldiers; tagged soldiers cannot be buffed, and any that die while tagged rise as weak minions on your side. The Tempest Rising notes give Subjugation a fit_note; the cut Subjugator and War Ender carry it too
patterns.hint: The fill agents called it convert-fallen-enemies (Vimana's Subjugation aura) and subjugate-infantry (the Enlightened's Subjugating Attack): one mechanic, Veti Subjugation. Check it is not a duplicate of mind-control, which takes living units.

patterns.summary: An effect stops enemies from using their active and passive abilities while it lasts, but leaves them free to move and attack; the Sentinel's EM Interference doctrine applies it to every enemy the GDF has Marked
patterns.hint: Proposed by the fill agent of job j05; check it against the weapon trait silence, which also stops firing.

patterns.summary: Arrive by pod, parachute or drop ship on a spot you choose, with a warning where you will land
patterns.hint: The Combat Chinook's fit_note asks for clearing an enemy-held building from above (troops dropped onto it kill the soldiers inside); decide whether that is a variant here or another id. William Mason's new suit crashing down at a chosen spot also uses it.

patterns.summary: Place two or more linked entrances, such as tunnel mouths or gates, that teammates enter at one and leave by another; destroying an entrance closes it
patterns.hint: The Thunderhead's fit_note: here the exit is the moving aircraft itself, not a second placed entrance, and losing the entrance kills everyone inside. Consider a variant.

patterns.summary: Let teammates respawn at or inside you, usually once you deploy somewhere safe
For a large price and a long cooldown, the unit brings a full, lasting unit (the Vimana's Caretaker) into play at its side, away from any factory; launch-drones covers only short-lived escorts
patterns.hint: Proposed by the fill agent of job j08.

patterns.summary: Spend resources during a life to add a weapon, module or armour to your current unit

Board a teammate's vehicle as extra crew to lift it to top rank while you ride, one per vehicle, and get thrown clear alive if it is destroyed. It may fold into passenger-sets-weapon as a rider who boosts rather than arms
patterns.hint: The fill agent called it join-vehicle-crew. Check against passenger-sets-weapon and rally-allies.

patterns.summary: When destroyed, the vehicle becomes a parked, fortified shell with fresh health instead of dying; riders survive hurt and fight on from it until the shell falls, and getting out ends it. It may fit better as an on_death term than as a pattern
patterns.hint: The fill agent linked passenger-sets-weapon's wreck-bunker variant and found no on_death term for the bunker. Decide whether this is a new id or that variant, and say which the Battle Bus should link.

patterns.summary: A lasting AI partner, usually an animal, fights beside you on its own and takes short orders such as attack or come back; it may heal allies (Anna's bear) or double as a mount (Olga's tiger). launch-drones releases expendable minions instead
Boost nearby teammates' fire rate, accuracy, speed or armour with an aura or a timed call
Refill teammates' ammo, energy or ability charges from a pack, crate or vehicle

Spend a cheap minion, or yourself, to give allies in an area a timed buff (less damage taken, more speed) plus a bonus that depends on each receiver: a reload, a repair, a summoned helper, wider sight or income
When an ally's buff lands on the unit, its spent ammunition comes back at once and refills faster while the buff lasts
patterns.hint: Proposed by the fill agent of job j08; resupply-allies is the pattern for the one who refills others. Decide whether this is a variant of resupply-allies or its own id.

patterns.summary: On a key, rake an area with heavy fire so enemies there slow down, aim badly and are pinned if they stay
Fill an area with smoke that blocks sight and aim for a short time
Fire one heavy special shot on a cooldown, often after a visible wind-up or by spending stored energy

While you stay put, a wide field around you slows the fire of every enemy rocket and missile weapon inside it, launchers and defences alike. Generals' ECM Tank (cut) makes missiles veer off instead, a deflect variant; fire-countermeasures is the on-key, self-only cousin
patterns.hint: The fill agent called it dampen-enemy-fire-aura: an always-on field that slows one kind of enemy weapon (rockets and missiles) while the unit stands still. Check against leave-hazard-zone and the zone weapon trait.

patterns.summary: Place an automatic turret or device that fights on its own
patterns.hint: The Shieldmaiden's fit_note asks for a placed device that works on its own without fighting (its repair turret), which deploy-turret, needing a device that fights, does not cover; William Mason's fit_note asks for recalling a parked machine (the empty suit rocket-jumps back to him). Decide variant or new id for each.

patterns.summary: Put up sandbags, wire, tank traps or walls that block shots or movement until destroyed

The unit lays down a building from a build menu, such as a headquarters, barracks or workshop, that then serves the team by training units or opening tech; it must go in an allowed zone and costs resources
patterns.hint: Proposed by the fill agent of job j13; build-cover is for cover pieces.

patterns.summary: On a key or as bought add-ons, release small drones or minions that fight around you and return or expire
On a key, repair or heal yourself, usually while standing still or by using up a limited kit
Feed on a harmful status that slows other vehicles and turn it into repairs, though the status's overload stage still hurts you
patterns.hint: The fill agent called it convert-debuff-to-health.

patterns.summary: A passive that raises your damage as your health falls, so a badly hurt unit is at its most dangerous and must be finished fast; the hero Lech Kos has it too

Anyone who attacks you from close by is zapped back automatically, so even an unarmed unit punishes attackers who come near. The Tempest Rising notes code it as a passive with a fit_note; it may suit an armour model or trait instead
patterns.hint: The fill agent called it retaliate-when-attacked (the Arcing passive).

patterns.summary: The unit cannot receive one hostile status (Tempest Charge) and mends itself inside the hazard field that would normally inflict it
patterns.hint: Proposed by the fill agent of job j08 (the Engine Tuning doctrine).

patterns.summary: A short burst of speed
patterns.hint: The Tempest Sphere's fit_note: its charge also crushes or rams whatever it meets on the way; consider a variant.

patterns.summary: Make yourself or allies immune to damage for a moment, at a cost
patterns.hint: The Aurora Bomber's fit_note asks for an attack-run variant: aimed fire misses a very fast plane during every run, not at a chosen moment. The trim proposed the id untouchable-attack-run for it; write that as a variant here unless it clearly needs its own id.

patterns.summary: Commit to a fast attack run during which nothing can hurt you, release one heavy payload, then leave slowed and exposed until you rearm. become-invulnerable is the nearest id, but there the timing is chosen rather than tied to the run
patterns.hint: Write this file only if it cannot be a variant of become-invulnerable; otherwise say so in open_points and write no file for it.

patterns.summary: Stop in place and earn money for the team without collecting anything, earning more with each rank gained by doing it; defenceless while working, so the enemy must find the earner. gather-resources needs a node and a route
patterns.hint: The fill agent called it earn-income-in-place; gather-resources needs a field and a route, and deploy-siege-mode covers only the set-up.

patterns.summary: Units of a set group improve (here they fire faster) while enough of them stand close together; no one unit gives the bonus, so thinning or splitting the group switches it off for all. The Generals notes rule out rally-allies; the swarm team-play hook covers the team side
patterns.hint: The fill agent called it group-up-for-bonus (the horde bonus); the Generals notes rule out rally-allies because no single unit raises the others.

patterns.summary: Many allied weapons stack a charge on enemy vehicles that slows them; at full stacks the vehicle overloads (damage over time, buttons off) and finisher weapons destroy it outright. A non-cryo cousin of freeze-and-shatter, built up by several teammates
patterns.hint: The Voltaic Tank's combos fit_note asks for a term for weapons that build a stacking status (Tempest Charge) that another unit cashes in; check against freeze-and-shatter.
